verbatim: AI services - selling access to AI tools, chatbots, image or content generation services, or subscriptions to AI services fulfilled outside of Gumroad
note: Selling a file an AI helped make is not covered. Describe the product as a file, not as a right to use a tool.

verbatim: While we support AI-assisted content we do not accept content that has been generated entirely by AI/LLMs that has not gone through extensive editing from a human.
note: The friendliest AI paragraph in this file. It is not what closes the shelf - see the next three rows.

verbatim: We may require further documentation of subject matter expertise for nonfiction content.
note: PARTIAL QUOTE for the companion sentence: accounts uploading nonfiction across several subjects are told they will need to "show proof of subject matter expertise around each topic" - fragment read inside a longer sentence we did not retain in full. Says nothing about AI; closes the shelf to an author who cannot document credentials.

disclosure_field: AI Generated by artist role in the book metadata, plus the description
clause: Formatting and Content Guidelines 1.13 - AI-generated content
verbatim: Book content that is AI-generated (i.e., a material portion of the content is generated by an AI-based tool as opposed to a human author), must be labeled as such using "AI Generated by" artist role and declaring the AI-generated creation method in the description.
note: The only shelf in this file that names a metadata role for the disclosure. Also on the same page: "Content that is AI-generated must explicitly state this in the description to avoid customer confusion."

clause: Formatting and Content Guidelines 1.13 - AI-assisted content
verbatim: AI-assisted content (i.e., AI has been used by a human author as a tool in idea generation, research, editing, refining text, or producing images for a book composed by a human author) does not require disclosure.
note: The sharpest AI-generated / AI-assisted boundary we have read anywhere in this file. The test is who composed the book, not which tool touched it.

clause: Create your account - what you need
verbatim: A U.S. tax ID if you're a company or a U.S.-based individual.
note: Entry is free - "The first thing you'll need to do is sign up for an account - it's free!" - and a non-US individual is not asked for a US tax ID. The sign-up itself still requires "an Apple Account with two-factor authentication and a valid credit card on file". Publisher type: "Select Individual if you're representing yourself or if you're a sole proprietor." No publisher-country list is published; the storefront list at /books/support/37-book-availability includes Japan.

verbatim: Books cannot contain prohibited explicit or objectionable content.
note: No list of refused subjects and no credential requirement for nonfiction. The two clauses that closed Draft2Digital to us have no counterpart here.

clause: metadata field in the product sheet
verbatim: Content Integrity Guidelines - AI and automated content
url: Books created using artificial intelligence (AI) or automated processes that are not correctly categorized using the metadata available in the product sheet, and/or containing erroneous or low-quality content.
column10: Also on the same page: "Low-quality books - text or images that contain errors, are poorly produced, incomplete, or have metadata or content issues that make the book difficult to understand." Correctly-tagged AI content is not refused; see the fee-tier row for why we declined anyway.

verbatim: Distribution plans - exclusivity
url: This plan is non-exclusive, allowing you to choose which platforms to activate or deactivate.
column10: Read first, ahead of the AI clause, because an exclusive terms clause would have conflicted with our already-open direct Apple Books channel. It did not; this is not what closed the shelf.

verbatim: Distribution plans - Basic and Pro pricing
url: Free forever, no hidden fees or subscription costs. ... this plan does not include Amazon or major retailers.
column10: PARTIAL QUOTE, two sentences from the Basic plan description joined with "...". Pro plan: "$99 per year" for access to "all our distribution partners, including the major international platforms". No store list is published for either plan; whether Kobo sits in Basic or Pro could not be confirmed from the primary source. The $99 fee is what actually closes this shelf under our $0 self-funding constraint.

verbatim: Create, modify, delete account
url: In StreetLib, authors and publishers located internationally (outside of Italy and Germany, Austria, and Switzerland) are subject to our membership plans.
column10: No nationality is named as refused. What "subject to our membership plans" means for a non-EU author (ordinary Basic/Pro choice, or something narrower) could not be settled from the primary source alone - not treated as fact either way. Also on the same page: "You must enter your real personal data, even if you will publish your books under a pseudonym (pen-name)."
